source: សៀវភៅ 'មធ្យោបាយប្រើប្រាស់ឧបករណ៍ព្រោះជាជួរ' (How to Use the Row/Drum Seeder Tool), presented by an agricultural extension teacher for the Agricultural Productivity Enhancement Project in the West Tonle Sap area (APPP) / CAVAC (Cambodia Agricultural Value Chain program), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries -- Battambang provincial department, 2014
text: The source compares seed quality/quantity needs for drum-seeder sowing versus ordinary hand broadcasting. Seed used with the drum seeder should be clean, not weed-contaminated, with husk not peeling/damaged, and germination not lost through poor storage; sowing broadcast without the tool uses roughly 80-100 kg/ha and wastes more seed through uneven placement, described as a 'lost yield/potential' outcome, while seed sown correctly through the drum seeder at the right rate is described as reliable with no such loss. The seed-metering drum has two hole-spacing options depending on the rice variety's tillering habit: for varieties with many tillers, sow at about 60-80 kg/ha through the wide-hole drum; for varieties with fewer tillers, sow at about 50-60 kg/ha through the narrow-hole drum. Both spacing options require the same quality standard: good germination, controlled moisture (not too wet or dried out), and freedom from weed seed.
